title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #214
gist: Packy McCormick's Weekly Dose #214 highlights Atomic Machines' Matter Compiler for micro-machine manufacturing, Anduril's $3.7B Arsenal-2 submarine-component shipyard, a Privo oral-cancer patch with 21/22 complete clearance, Biohub's $1.8B virtual-cell data push, and this year's Nobel winners.

insights.claim: Atomic Machines emerged from six years in stealth with the Matter Compiler, an AI-native system that builds working micro-machines from code with no per-product tooling or process development.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Potential new manufacturing platform for MEMS-class devices; early-stage and company-claimed.

insights.claim: Atomic Machines' first product, the PrimeSwitch PS-150, is a 9.5 mm relay carrying 150 amps that opens in 50 microseconds, about 1,000x faster than a contactor, aimed at the 800-volt DC data centers AI is driving.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Power-switching bottleneck for AI data-center power architecture; early customer shipments just starting.
insights.locator: The first product AM is building

insights.claim: MEMS were a $15.4 billion market across 31 billion units in 2024, and Atomic Machines argues existing chip-fab toolsets limit what micro-machines can be made, so a code-driven process opens new categories like sand-grain gears, in-body robots, AI-chip cooling and instant blood tests.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Addressable market framing for micro-manufacturing startups.

insights.claim: An a16z chart cited says each $100 into the AI buildout supply chain splits about $50 to chips, $20 to power, $15 to networking and $15 to cooling, buildings and land.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Shows where AI capex dollars land; power is the second-largest bucket.

insights.claim: Anduril will invest $3.7 billion in Arsenal-2, a two-million-square-foot 'software-defined shipyard' at Sparrows Point, Maryland making Virginia-class submarine components, creating over 3,100 jobs with production targeted for 2030 and a California start in 2028.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Private capital building defense shipbuilding capacity; Anduril is an investor-disclosed holding of the author.

insights.claim: The US Navy awarded Anduril a contract worth up to $2.9 billion with payments tied to demonstrated production outcomes, meaning Anduril funds capacity first and is paid as it delivers; torpedo tubes are already holding up submarines under construction.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Outcome-based procurement shifts capex risk to contractor and addresses submarine supply chain bottlenecks.

insights.claim: Privo's PRV111 cisplatin patch cleared lesions completely in 21 of 22 patients with non-invasive oral cancer or high-grade precancer in a Phase 2 study, all 22 avoided planned surgery, with no recurrences at 14 months median follow-up and negligible systemic exposure.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Small Phase 2; positive early signal for local drug delivery replacing surgery.

insights.claim: Biohub announced an expanded $1.8 billion collaboration to build datasets for predictive virtual-cell models, with Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs and Meta investing $300 million alongside DOE and NIH contributions.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Big-tech participation signals virtual cells as a drug-discovery data race.

insights.claim: The 2026 Nobel in Physiology or Medicine went to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for optogenetics, with Physics to Francis Halzen (IceCube neutrinos) and Chemistry to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai (asymmetric synthesis autocatalysis).
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick

insights.claim: Packy produced a short film, KILO, by giving his essay and direction to Claude/ChatGPT to orchestrate production with Runway, illustrating that long-form writing can be turned into film in a few prompts.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Creator-economy tooling is collapsing the cost of media production.
